episode.tagline: Songs, albums, books, films are the way they for a reason -- and those reasons are outdated. The dominant forms of creative expression evolved because of constraints that no longer apply. We should free our minds and look beyond them!

items.content: Ajay opens by calling Amit 'more than just an atom in a kinetic theory of gases' since he also contemplates the theory. Amit: 'If I was…
On the ten-and-a-half-hour episode. Ajay: 'I'm still waiting for my gold medal.' Amit: 'until the podcast comes to an end, you can't get…
Pointing out the birdsong in the background: 'The twittering of birds, not twitter... or perhaps we should call the Xing of birds.'
On rainforest birds that repeat the same narrow-frequency call so something gets through: 'Like so many columnists, in fact.'
On why open-air processions are percussive: 'You will not hear khayals and thumris while people are marching to the beach.'
Amit's off-colour aside about the author of Der Edelstein: 'Apparently his wife used to say that every morning I wake up and I find that…
On early crooners singing softly into the mic: 'much as some podcasters can do with their dynamic microphones.'
Amit calls the mushaira newsletters exposure to 'a large LLM, as it were', using AI vocabulary for a 19th-century reader's sample size.
On binge-watching: 'For those of us who have office, we miss office the next day. I don't have to.'
Amit says the mediocre artist is 'starving in an attic as the cliche goes.' Ajay: 'therefore it's called having a girlfriend with a job.'
Ajay: 'owing to the shortage of followers, the production of leaders has been discontinued.' Amit objects that not everyone is a…
Winston Churchill, quoted by Ajay: 'we make our buildings and then our buildings make us.'
Stephen Covey: 'we listen to respond, we don't listen to understand.' Amit uses it to describe the listening long conversations require.
Stewart Brand, quoted by Ajay: 'We are as gods and we might as well learn to live like that.'
Malcolm Gladwell's 10,000 hours, applied to the Beatles' Hamburg years around 1962.
'It ain't over till the fat lady sings', used to explain why opera singers had to project before the microphone.
Sturgeon's Law, 'ninety five percent of everything is crap', which Amit cites while arguing that great art is still being made in…
The Doordarshan-era half-hour TV show: 24 minutes of content plus two 3-minute ad breaks.
Timothy Snyder's On Tyranny, about 12,000 words, as the rare short book a great writer can get away with.
Amit calls Bari Weiss 'a fellow winner of the Bastiat Prize.'
The Peter Cat Recording Company, loved by Amit and crew Nomsita and Vaishnav: 'never gonna be the Beatles in terms of scale', but the…
The era of building temples to Amitabh Bachchan, which Amit thinks we may have seen the last of as fame moves into niches.
